Brand narrative

Seen is not the same as understood

Short answer

A brand narrative is the story that explains why your company exists, what it does differently, and why the right buyers should choose it. Many B2B companies are visible but not understood: their message makes sense inside the company, but sounds like everyone else outside it. A clear narrative gives every team, channel and partner the same story to tell.

Is this you?

  • People know your name, but can’t say what makes you different
  • Your website, pitch deck and sales conversations tell different stories
  • Your message sounds like every competitor’s: modern, innovative, trusted, premium
  • Each new campaign starts from a blank page
  • Senior decision-makers don’t remember what you said after the meeting

Why it happens

Inside a company, everyone knows what it does and why it matters, so the message gets written for people who already understand. Outside, buyers meet that message without context, among many others that sound alike.

In crowded markets, the safest-sounding words become the most common ones. Looking right is not the same as standing out.

How I work on this

  1. Listen: the company’s real story, from leadership, teams and, where possible, clients
  2. Diagnose: how your current message is heard, and where it blends in with competitors
  3. Narrative: the core story, the proof behind it, and how it adapts for each audience
  4. System: how the narrative reaches every touchpoint, from website and sales materials to events and partners

What you get

  • A clear core narrative and messaging framework
  • Key messages for each priority audience
  • Proof points that make the story credible
  • Guidance for teams and agencies so everyone tells the same story

FAQs

Is this copywriting?

No. Copywriting expresses a message. This work decides what the message should be. Once the narrative is clear, your team or agency writes from it, or I direct the specialists who do.

How is this different from a brand strategy?

It is part of it. The narrative is the part of brand strategy that decides what the market should understand about you, and it is often the part that’s missing.
